en.name: Adeodatus II
en.summary: A Roman monk of St. Erasmus whose brief, largely uneventful pontificate fell in the quiet interlude between the Byzantine-dominated seventh century's theological storms.
en.body: Little is recorded of Adeodatus II's four-year reign beyond his monastic background and a reputation for personal kindness toward the poor, including a practice of distributing alms with his own hands. He governed during a lull between the Monothelite controversy that had convulsed his predecessors and the disputes that would follow, and no major councils or conflicts are securely attributed to him. His pontificate is chiefly notable for how little survives about it, typical of the sparse record-keeping of Rome under Byzantine exarchate rule.
